description: Deed dated August 20, 1906, in which Lazarus B. Wilson and his wife, Annie B. Wilson, of Baltimore City, Maryland, conveyed a parcel of land on Deals Island in Somerset County, Maryland, to Mrs. Addie L. Webster for $250. The property was described as part of a five-acre parcel formerly belonging to William Evans and land formerly belonging to Joseph Beauchamp. According to the Wilson-Daniel family tree, the grantor was Lazarus Benjamin Wilson (1857–1922), the maternal uncle of Addie Leola Daniel Webster (1881–1922). Lazarus and Addie's mother, Mary Catherine Wilson (1859–1910), were children of Samuel David Wilson (1823–1914). The deed documents a property transaction between Lazarus and Addie, while the family relationship is identified through genealogical research and awaits independent corroboration.

title: 1930 United States Federal Census – Adam Kramer and Snead Webster Families
location: Luzerne Avenue, Ward 4, Baltimore City, Maryland, United States
description: The Fifteenth Census of the United States, 1930, Maryland, Baltimore City, Ward 4, Enumeration District 4-532, Sheet 6A, enumerated April 2, 1930. Lines 18–19 record Adam Kramer (age 26) and his wife Sue Kramer (recorded age 26). Lines 20–22 record the immediately following household, headed by Snead Webster (age 58), with his sons Charles Webster (age 21) and Wilson Webster (age 10). Snead Webster was William Gabriel Snead Webster, father of Sue, Charles, and Wilson. The two households were located next to one another on Luzerne Avenue in Baltimore. The census records Sue as age 26, although her reported birth date of October 22, 1902, would make her 27 at the time of enumeration. This record establishes that Charles and Wilson were living in their father's household in April 1930, providing important context for research into the Webster children's living arrangements following the death of their mother, Addie Leola Daniel Webster, in 1922.

title: 1939 Maryland Death Certificate – William Gabriel Snead Webster
description: Baltimore City Health Department Certificate of Death No. 57236 records the death of William Gabriel Snead Webster on April 17, 1939, at 200 North Glover Street, Baltimore, Maryland. The certificate identifies him as George Gabriel Snead Webster, gives his birth date as June 29, 1877, names his father as George Webster and his mother as Mary Katharine (surname unknown), and identifies his wife and informant as Mrs. Eloise L. Webster. Family research identifies his correct name as William Gabriel Snead Webster and his parents as Gabriel S. Webster and Susan A. Windsor. The certificate identifies his occupation as carpenter, notes his retirement from WPA employment, and records burial at Woodlawn Cemetery on April 20, 1939. The original certificate is preserved as issued, including its conflicting information.

These names correspond to Gabriel Snead Webster and Addie Leola Daniel in the family archive. Her marital status is recorded as widowed, and Adam Kramer is named as her spouse. The certificate identifies Woodlawn Cemetery in Baltimore, Maryland, as her burial location. Bette Singletary is listed as the informant.

title: 1871 Newspaper Report – Typhoid Deaths in the Snead Webster Family
description: Newspaper clipping under the heading 'SOMERSET,' from an unidentified newspaper and publication date. The article reports that Snead Webster and his son Snead, residents of Deal's Island, died within hours of each other on Monday the 11th of the publication month. A younger son reportedly died the preceding Thursday. The article attributes all three deaths to typhoid fever. Family research identifies the sons as Newton Snead Webster and Elmer Webster, but the clipping does not give their full names. The publication is believed to date from 1871; the exact month and newspaper remain to be established.
supports: Snead Webster and a son also called Snead died within hours of each other.

title: 1902 Obituary of James T. Daniel
location: Wenona, Deal Island, Somerset County, Maryland
description: Newspaper obituary reporting the death of James T. Daniel at his residence in Wenona, Deal Island, in February 1902. The obituary describes his involvement in the Prohibition Party, his participation in state and county conventions, and his consideration for the Maryland State Senate. It states that he was twice married and was survived by his widow and thirteen children. The newspaper title and publication date have not yet been independently verified.

title: Daniel Family — Genealogical History
location: Rowan County, North Carolina; Somerset County, Maryland
description: Privately compiled family genealogy titled The Daniel Name, probably prepared by Daniel Leroy Drake, son of Anna Wilson Daniel Drake and grandson of James Fairfax Daniel. The author identifies Anna Wilson Daniel as his mother, describes personally knowing James Fairfax Daniel, and references family records in his possession. The genealogy traces the Daniel family from Rowan County, North Carolina, to Deal Island, Maryland, and documents later generations of the Daniel, Drake, Webster, and related families. The latest date identified in the document is 1977, suggesting compilation or revision no earlier than that year. Copies were circulated among family members. According to family recollection, a copy was held by the Kramer-Webster family during the 1980s and certainly before 1993. The exact author attribution, compilation date, and original distribution date have not been independently verified.

title: DAR Ancestor Record — James Daniel (A029613)
description: Daughters of the American Revolution ancestor record A029613 for James Daniel, also recorded as James Daniels. The DAR recognizes his Revolutionary War patriotic service in North Carolina through furnishing money and supplies. The ancestor information identifies his birth as approximately 1755 in Northumberland County, Virginia, and his death as February 11, 1817, in Rowan County, North Carolina. The record references North Carolina Revolutionary War accounts as supporting documentation. The DAR birth estimate differs from the 1752 birth year used in the family genealogy and should be evaluated against original records.

Archival references cited in the DAR documentation for James Daniel's patriotic service include North Carolina Revolutionary Army Accounts, Volume XII, Book A, Part XII, page 1631; and Accounts of the United States with North Carolina for the Revolutionary War, Book C, page 151, Roll S.115.45. These references are retained as research leads. The original account entries have not yet been independently located or examined.

Patriotic service through furnishing money and supplies in North Carolina

title: Maryland Militia in the War of 1812 – Travis Daniel, Somerset County
description: Maryland Militia in the War of 1812, Volume 1 (Eastern Shore Counties), PDF page 11, printed page 4. Under the Tenth Brigade, a detachment return from the 23rd Regiment of the Somerset County Militia lists 'Travis Daniel' among the privates of the 2nd Battalion. The return refers to division orders dated May 15, but the year of those orders is not specified in the excerpt. Travis Daniel is believed to be Travers Daniel (1780–1861), whose given name also appears as Traverse in other historical records. The identification is supported by family research and a previous inquiry concerning a commemorative wreath for his gravestone at Daniel Family Cemetery, Wenona, Maryland. The roster does not establish the duration of his service or participation in combat.

The detachment was associated with the Tenth Brigade of the Maryland Militia.
The return was prepared pursuant to orders dated May 15.

title: William Daniel, Candidate for Vice President
description: Historical newspaper biographical article titled 'William Daniel, Candidate for Vice President.' Describes William Daniel as a resident of Mount Washington in Baltimore County, Maryland, born on Deal Island in Somerset County. Identifies him as a practicing attorney who began practicing law in Baltimore in 1860, a Union supporter during the Civil War, a former member of the Maryland House of Delegates and State Senate, and a leading advocate of temperance and prohibition. The article discusses his organization and presidency of the Maryland State Temperance Alliance and his nomination for vice president. The newspaper name, publication date, and page number have not yet been established.
